proof_skeleton_nl: Start by translating polynomiality of Q_{A,B,d}(q) into cyclotomic multiplicity inequalities. Upgrade those inequalities to a Hall-type semigroup condition saying that every coordinate subset J sees at least |J| accessible target degrees. Invoke the weighted existence theorem to choose homogeneous equations of degrees A+1,...,A+d whose common zero set is only the origin. By Nullstellensatz the quotient is Artinian, and since the ambient ring is a positively graded polynomial ring of dimension d, those d homogeneous equations form a regular sequence. The standard Hilbert-series formula then gives exactly Q_{A,B,d}(q).

steps.derives: If d = 0, then the theorem holds: S=Q, Q_{A,B,0}(q)=1, and the empty sequence is a homogeneous regular sequence whose quotient has Hilbert series 1.
steps.trivial_justification: Lemma L7 is exactly the required statement in the empty-variable case.

steps.derives: Assume d > 0 and Q_{A,B,d}(q) belongs to Q[q]. Then for every positive integer n, the divisibility-count inequality #{ j in {1,...,d} : n divides (B+j) } <= #{ e in {A+1,...,A+d} : n divides e } holds.
steps.trivial_justification: This is the forward implication of Lemma L1 applied to the given polynomiality assumption.

steps.derives: Assume d > 0. For every nonempty subset J of {1,...,d}, if Sigma(J) = { sum_{j in J} m_j (B+j) : m_j in Z_{>=0} }, then at least |J| of the integers A+1,...,A+d lie in Sigma(J).
steps.trivial_justification: Step B2 supplies exactly the hypotheses of Lemma L2, so Lemma L2 yields the Hall-type semigroup condition for the weights B+1,...,B+d and degrees A+1,...,A+d.

steps.derives: Assume d > 0. There exist homogeneous polynomials g_1,...,g_d in S=Q[x_1,...,x_d] with deg(g_i)=A+i such that, over an algebraic closure of Q, the common zero locus of g_1,...,g_d in affine d-space is exactly the origin.
steps.trivial_justification: Apply Lemma L3 with k=Q, weights w_j=B+j, and target degrees e_i=A+i. The field Q is infinite, and Step B3 verifies the required Hall-type semigroup hypothesis.

steps.derives: Assume d > 0. The quotient S/(g_1,...,g_d) is finite-dimensional over Q.
steps.trivial_justification: This is the direct conclusion of Lemma L4 applied to the homogeneous ideal I=(g_1,...,g_d), using the zero-locus statement from Step B4.

steps.derives: Assume d > 0. The sequence g_1,...,g_d is a homogeneous regular sequence in S; equivalently, for each i the image of g_i in S/(g_1,...,g_{i-1}) is not a zero-divisor.
steps.trivial_justification: Step B4 provides homogeneity of the d elements and Step B5 provides finite-dimensionality of the quotient, so Lemma L5 applies immediately.

steps.derives: Assume d > 0. Setting f_i := g_i for i=1,...,d gives homogeneous elements f_1,...,f_d in S with deg(f_i)=A+i, and for each i the image of f_i in S/(f_1,...,f_{i-1}) is not a zero-divisor.
steps.trivial_justification: This is a direct renaming of the elements from Steps B4 and B6.

steps.derives: Assume d > 0. The quotient by the constructed sequence satisfies Hilb_{S/(f_1,...,f_d)}(q) = prod_{i=1}^d (1-q^(A+i)) / prod_{i=1}^d (1-q^(B+i)) = Q_{A,B,d}(q).
steps.trivial_justification: Apply Lemma L6 with weights w_i=B+i and degrees e_i=A+i, then substitute the definition of Q_{A,B,d}(q).

steps.derives: For integers A, B, d with A >= B >= 0 and d >= 0, define Q_{A,B,d}(q) := prod_{i=1}^d (1 - q^(A+i)) / (1 - q^(B+i)), with the empty product equal to 1 when d = 0. Assume Q_{A,B,d}(q) belongs to Q[q]. Let S be the weighted polynomial ring Q[x_1, ..., x_d] graded by deg(x_i) = B+i; when d = 0 interpret S as Q. Then there exist homogeneous polynomials f_1, ..., f_d in S such that deg(f_i) = A+i for every i, and for each i the image of f_i in S/(f_1, ..., f_{i-1}) is not a zero-divisor. Equivalently, Q_{A,B,d}(q) is realized by a homogeneous regular sequence in a weighted polynomial ring with variable weights B+1, ..., B+d and relation degrees A+1, ..., A+d.
steps.trivial_justification: Use Step B1 for d=0. For d>0, Step B7 gives the required regular sequence in the specified degrees, and Step B8 gives the claimed realization of Q_{A,B,d}(q) as the Hilbert-series quotient associated to that regular sequence.
